utterances.text: Let me ask you the question again; I'm sorry about that. I'm right in saying that you walked around Grubori with Mr. Turkalj on the 27th [Realtime error read in error "25th"] of August of 1995, sometime after midday?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now, as for the time-period when we were in Grubori, I cannot say where that was after midday. I can assume that if we were in Gracac at 7.00 we went to Grubori straight away, so as for this entire visit, it was during the course of the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If I may just, there is a mistake on the record. It should be on the 26th.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: 27th.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: 27th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Just to establish with you once again, on the 27th of August you walked around Grubori at some time during the day with Mr. Turkalj, is that right? That's the person that you remember walking with you around Grubori, right?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. However, may I explain? The two of us were not on our own. It was a group of people there. But since he was my superior, I was with him all the time. That is to say that my tour of Grubori was with him, throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, if you could look at your statement here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This is -- and if we could please go -- this is page 13765, and if we could go to the bottom of that page -- I think this is actually the wrong page. Is this page 21 of V00-2126?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It is actually 4126, for the record. That's a mistake on the top of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Oh, 4126. It's a mistake on the page. I need page 21, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Let's just move ahead so that we don't waste any time. Your memory of Mr. Cermak being in Grubori on that day is him standing in the village with a camera crew. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we can't find that page, we can actually move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The page number is in the English copies are at the top so if you just take the cursor --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It's page -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You got the wrong --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yeah, it's 4124.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: 4124. It should be 4126.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We can move ahead if it is the wrong one. If we could please have 65 ter 3169, which I think now is exactly an exhibit, and is P772.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Celic, I want to talk about events after you left Grubori, and I want to talk about this lunch in Knin itself and the meeting that you say took place before that lunch where Mr. Sacic spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And if we can please go to the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And this is the statement or the Official Note from your interview from 2001 where you speak of your visit to Grubori. Now, I don't dispute the fact that you say you may have had lunch in Knin; we all remember a good lunch. But in this Official Note, there is no mention whatsoever, is there, of a meeting which took place in Knin on the 27th of August, after you visited Grubori?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. In this Official Note, it is quite evident -- well, actually I was sure at the time whether we went to Knin first or whether we went to visit Grubori first. You can see this report, but during the examination I have stated that I cannot say exactly what the time was. Now I'm making an assumption in view of all of these facts that it was lunch-time, first Grubori and then Knin and then this says something different, but then that is what I thought at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So in 2001 you couldn't recall the lunch or the meeting in Knin on the 27th of August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to that because there is a reference to the party going to Knin and it says to see General Cermak. Now that has not been elaborated in this but it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you may lead a witness, of course, Mr. Cayley. However, there are limits to what you could lead him, if there are clear points of reference. Now, it is it not lunch and a meeting but it is a person. Could you please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, in your interview of November of 2002, and you can take this from me, there is no reference at all to this meeting in Knin. Now, again, I don't dispute the fact that you may have had lunch in Knin. Were you aware, do you recall that in the garrison headquarters there was a public kitchen where soldiers and other individuals after the fall of Knin would take communal meals together? Do you recall that location in Knin?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the way I'm going to put it. I just have to distinguish between different things. We did not have headquarters of a unit. We had headquarters where all the specials were. If it was -- if we were out in the field we usually had lunch packages. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you were asked about whether you were aware of a public kitchen where soldiers and other individuals, after the fall of Knin, would take communal meals together. Are you aware or are you not, of this public kitchen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not aware of that. Not. If you allow me, what I was trying to say in response to your previous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first wait what the next question of Mr. Cayley will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So you can't recall specifically where you had lunch in Knin. You can just recall you had lunch in Knin somewhere?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you misunderstood what I said. I don't remember that there was a public kitchen for soldiers in Knin, but I do remember the building where we had our meals. Whether this was a public kitchen for soldiers, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If, please, we could have P762. And if we could please have page 118 of 212, and that's ERN number 5276. That's the wrong one again. Page -- I'm told it is page 429.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You got the wrong page. There is no page 429 of any of the sections.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Sorry, I was told -- oh, I'm told I'm right. Everybody's telling me I'm right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 429 is a number which could, if you use the Adobe reproduction, then it numbers throughout, whereas I'm not aware of any 429 in any other format but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Anyway if it could be scrolled down, and the only part I want you to look at, up at the -- yeah, and this is -- I'm having to move quickly through this, Mr. Celic, because I don't have much time, but if you see where you say, "No, I remember when we came to Knin we went to the building where General Cermak was and I recall that we had lunch there all together." Now, again, I am not disputing that you had lunch in Knin, but you will see there is no reference of any kind of meeting with Mr. Sacic speaking, is there, as you testified yesterday?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, we had a conversation. Whether you would refer to this as meetings or not, I don't know. But we discussed everything that had happened in Grubori. I was expected to say where I was and what we did. I did. But Sacic had some other information and this is what we discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So in fact what you're saying now is that you would not refer to what you say took place as a meeting at all. Based on your recollection.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said I don't know what you would refer to this as, but we were there together. We discussed all this. And I assume that was a meeting or would qualify as a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Let us take a look at page 13311 -- sorry 13310; my apologies. 113, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Page 424, if that helps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We just changed from registrar. I think he must be in a state of complete confusion, not having attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This is the last one, Your Honour. My word on that. It's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, this is the same interview and it is the only other reference to this event that we're talking about and you can see there at line 14: "After that we went to Knin, we went to lunch, it was the building where General Cermak was staying." And again you'll note there is absolutely no reference to any meeting at all. Do you see that? There is no reference to a meeting taking place before lunch. Do you see that? And then I have a question for you after that. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So what I'm putting to you, Mr. Celic, is this. You have not mentioned in any of the statements that you have made to the OTP or your statement, the Official Note of your statement to the Croatian MUP in 2001 that there was ever a meeting preceding your lunch in Knin, and I'm putting it to you that you are mistaken about that, that there was no such meeting.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not have said -- I couldn't say this precisely, and I'll tell you why. During the interview, the investigators did not give me a time-frame when they asked the questions, and I couldn't really talk about the exact time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you. When you told us about this meeting, Mr. Cayley suggests that since you've never talked about a meeting, irrespective of the exact time, that you may have been mistaken when you told us about this meeting. Is that something that you accept or is that something that you do not accept, that it was a mistake, what you told us about the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I just wanted to clarify the following, because we are referring back to my 2005 statements and the Official Note. It is it evident from this statement or this note that I first went to Knin and then only to Grubori. I recall very well that we did go to Knin. So this is not at issue. There is no lacunae at any point whether we did go or not. We did go to Knin around lunch-time and obviously based on all the other events, this happened after Grubori and not, in other words, during lunch-time. And we were there and that's where we discussed this and this was a meeting. I would call it meeting. We had lunch there and we discussed this there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Celic, I'm putting it to you because we dispute what you are saying, that there was no meeting and there was certainly no meeting between you, Mr. Sacic, and Mr. Cermak.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only speak for myself and for what I know about. We did come to Knin, we came to this building, we had lunch there and we discussed it. Specifically Mr. Sacic asked me to tell him what I knew about this and I told him that I knew nothing. So in Knin, Mr. Sacic and I did discuss this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You're not actually answering my question and I'll put it to you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, I think your question was more or less repetitious --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to mine, and I think the answer of the witness is -- if you want to put it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No. I'm told there's a translation error. He said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: About the sequence?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No, I'm not -- he said "I suppose there was a meeting," not "I would call it a meeting."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, how do you suppose that something is a meeting? You -- Mr. Celic, you considered this to be a meeting, when you were in that room, as you said, Mr. Sacic spoke most. You considered this a meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if we sat there together and discussed this, if you want to call it a briefing or a debriefing or a meeting, call it whatever you will but I can tell you that we did talk about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, you say that you spoke with Mr. Sacic. Now, you did not speak with Mr. Cermak, did you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not personally. I personally did not discuss this with Mr. Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And, in fact, Mr. Cermak was not present at this meeting with you and Mr. Sacic, was he?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived there, we were all together. And at one point I have a clear recollection of this, I did see Mr. Cermak. But I don't want to provide false information. Whether he was there throughout or left at some point, I -- I couldn't tell you, but I remember that we had lunch together in this building and I think this was the command of the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So whilst you saw Mr. Cermak, as you sit here now, you cannot be sure that he was at that meeting, can you, with you and Mr. Sacic?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I object to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That question has been answered in quite some detail. The witness answered quite detailed questions about this matter before and it is inappropriate to put it to him in this way, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cayley. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I dont have re-examination, but just to clarify for the record, at page 107, line 2 to 11 the witness has given in two paragraphs an answer and it is contradictory. I just want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the issue where I expected that there might have been a translation problem. I'm not saying there is. Mr. Celic, at a certain moment, you said that you went to Knin after you had gone to Grubori. That's your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because in one of your previous answers, unlike, I would say, most, if not all of the other answers, you put it the other way around, that you first were in Knin and then to Grubori. In that same paragraph you later said: "We first went to Grubori and then to Knin." The last one is the right version, is it, or is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so. I couldn't say exactly until I was given some other information by the investigators but this was my error in the first Official Note. I was convinced that it had been the other way around but then, after the subsequent information I considered it to be otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what was that information that you made change your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the interview with the investigators when they asked me at what time I came to Gracac, where I was and so on, and from the evidence of other witnesses, it became obvious that we did not go to Knin first but rather to Grubori, because the others were certain that that's how it transpired and I was not. But now I am fairly certain, almost 99 per cent that it was first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... who were those other witnesses, Mr. Celic, and how did you learn about what those other witnesses said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think Mr. Balunovic's statement and Mr. Turkalj's statement and according to them, we were all supposed to be there together and we went to Grubori first and then to Knin for lunch. But since we are talking about lunch, then we must have gone to Grubori first. That is how I came to the conclusion that it was Grubori first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when you say the statements of Mr. Balunovic and -- it says on the transcript Turkalj -- oh, I don't know whether I -- Those statements were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- given to whom? Were these statements given to the Croatian authorities or were these statements given to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the investigators asked me to tell them the time-line when we went through it together, I wasn't able to pinpoint the time. But during their questioning, they read out to me quotes from certain statements, and then I was able to orient myself more easily about the time, so I received this information from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do apologise for interrupting you. May I ask -- based on what you asked, could I ask two or three questions of the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have one or two questions as well. Ms. Mahindaratne, still no questions. Mr. Mikulicic, still no questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will have a couple of questions, within two minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two minutes. Then I suggest that we take the usual order, if there are questions by the Bench at this moment, and then give a last opportunity to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Celic, I have two questions for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first is the occasion at which you made your -- you wrote your third report, you said it would be most likely 1st of September in Zagreb, is nowhere mentioned in your statement to the Croatian authorities, was it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made no such statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you reviewed during the break a report in which you said your statement to the Croatian authorities was actually reflected, and you made one correction. In those reports, we do not find anything about this 1st of September gathering and producing a new report, a few lines added, typed out by the secretary, do we?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I may have missed something. Then I would apologise if I put a question to you that you have answered already. We have very much focussed on the 25th of August, the 25th and 26th of August operations. Now, how many operations clearing the terrain in total your unit has done, well, let's say in the month of August and September?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In August and September, well, the first one at the beginning of August was Storm. Then in mid August there was operation Obruc in the area of Petrova Gora and on the 25th and 26th was Oluja-Obruc in the area of Gospic. I think that all these operations were in the month of August. As for September, I think we really didn't have any but we could look at the war path to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Mr. Mikulicic, I think is in terms of the order the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic. Further cross-examination by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Celic, the purpose of your conversation and your arrival in Gospic [as interpreted] in the headquarters on the 26th was obviously that in relation to Grubori there are different versions of the events concerned. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Sacic as head of the headquarters of the special police was obviously given a task by General Markac who was there to establish what it that had actually happened. Was that your understanding of the matter?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my understanding of the matter because I only talked to him about this and I received this information from him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... that task?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I could just point out the -- there's a reference to Gospic. It should be Gracac, not Gospic. Your arrival in Gospic in the headquarters in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should have been Gracac, yes. Thank you. I think there is no confusion about the meeting. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mr. Sacic got that task from General Markac because obviously General Markac wanted to establish the truth no matter what it was. Is your understanding of the matter?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say anything about the relationship between Mr. Markac and Mr. Sacic. I can say about them and me it was my understanding only that Mr. Sacic is in charge of that part, that he was trying to see what had happened, because I only communicated with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Do you know that Mr. Sacic before you, on that day in Gracac, talked to someone else about the incident in Grubori?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And it is correct, Mr. Celic, that the civilian police was informed about the incident in Grubori at that time. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in view of the meeting, or rather the visit to Grubori, where the policemen were present obviously they did know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And it is right, Mr. Celic, isn't it, that the crime police of the civilian police carried out an investigation and informed the public prosecutor if a crime had been committed as to who the suspects were so that the public prosecutor could decide to issue an indictment before the relevant Court, is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was wondering to what extent these questions were a follow-up on anything that happened before you cross-examined the witness. Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two or three questions, you said. I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I will be very quick, Your Honour. Further cross-examination by Mr. Cayley:

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Celic, you said a moment ago to His Honour Judge Orie that when the OTP investigators asked you to tell the time-line, when we went through it together you weren't able to pinpoint the time. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I couldn't say exactly what the relevant times were. Quite simply because so much time had elapsed, I couldn't say what the exact time had been.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So they read to you the statements of other witnesses in order to help you orientate yourself in time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Otherwise, throughout the interview I did my best to say the truth and nothing but the truth and that is what I'm doing now and I will give you a specific example that I've just remembered. The question was when I met up with Mr. Sacic was it the 25th or 26th. I could not give an accurate answer. However, when it was read out to me that Mr. Sacic made a statement to the effect that he certainly was not in Gracac and Knin on the 25th, that he was in Zagreb then, that he came only on the 26th, then I only could have confirmed that it was probably on the 26th because after that all that time, I couldn't know. I simply could not tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And you recall the statements of Mr. Balunovic and Mr. Turkalj being read to you by the OTP investigators. Yes?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot tell you very specifically now whether that is what they read out, but during the interview itself, with them I mean, and with Mr. Balunovic, I can say or rather I could have provided exact information. However, when I talked to the investigators what was really helpful was that, so I was as specific as I could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, in respect to these witness statements that were read to you --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just point out this -- the entire two interviews are on record and Mr. Cayley is aware of exactly what has been read to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, that was also why I had some hesitations to put all these questions to the witness but I did put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could I ask when more question, Your Honour, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What was the name of the investigator that read these statements to you. Was it Mr. Casey?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP CELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no further questions ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no further questions, Mr. Celic, this concludes your evidence in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for having answered all the questions, questions put to you by the parties, questions put to you by the Bench and I wish you a safe trip home again. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Celic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we adjourn I would like to express my appreciation to all who made it possible to conclude the testimony of the witness today. That is interpreters, transcribers, security, technical assistance, registry representatives. I would like to thank you very much. We adjourn until Monday, the 8th of September, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom III.
